newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH CAR SALES JUMP NEARLY 41 PCT IN 1996.
newsitem.headline: POLISH CAR SALES JUMP NEARLY 41 PCT IN 1996.

text.p: New car sales in Poland soared 40.9 percent last year, showing the biggest growth rate in Europe, an independent monitoring agency reported on Friday.
A monthly survey by the private Samar agency, which monitors the domestic car market, showed 373,542 new passenger cars were registered last year, compared with 265,038 in 1995.
The number of newly-registered delivery vehicles jumped by nearly 62.2 percent to 51,812 units in 1996.
The survey showed that 116,399 vehicles were imported.
Samar, quoting figures from the Association des Constructeurs Europeens d'Automobiles, said Poland had the fastest new car sales growth rate in Europe.
It said Poland was followed by Norway and Ireland, where car registration growth reached 38.1 percent and 32.3 percent over the period, with 125,000 and 115,100 cars sold respectively.
Germany, the leader in new car sales volume, registered an estimated 3,508,300 passenger cars last year, 5.9 percent more than in 1995.
In Poland, the domestic unit of Fiat Spa led the market with 155,857 cars and nearly 42 percent market share.
Other top sellers included Daewoo-FSO, a unit of South Korea's Daewoo Corp, General Motors' German unit Adam Opel AG and Renault.
Analysts say that robust car sales were fuelled by growth in real wages and expansion of credit by banks.
